name: Fall Creek Falls State Park
unique: One of the largest state parks in Tennessee, with four major waterfalls in a gorge cut into the Cumberland Plateau, including Fall Creek Falls dropping 256 feet, the highest free falling waterfall in the eastern United States.
buzz: The main overlook is a short walk and the gorge trail down to the base is steep and worth it. Summer weekends are busy, October is the photograph.

name: Fall Creek Falls Suspension Bridge
unique: A swinging footbridge over Cane Creek gorge on the trail between the falls overlooks, hanging high enough above the water that people stop halfway to look down.
buzz: Kids love it and adults grip the cables. The bridge is the photo from the park that ends up on social media.

name: Pikeville Courthouse Square
unique: One of the older county seats in Tennessee, with the courthouse and a small commercial block in the valley below the plateau, on the road that leads up to the falls.
buzz: A ten minute stop on the way to Fall Creek Falls. The square is quiet and the courthouse is the building.

name: Cumberland Mountain State Park
unique: A Civilian Conservation Corps park built in the 1930s around Byrd Lake, with a stone dam, rustic cabins and the remains of the homesteads that failed on this thin plateau soil.
buzz: The CCC stonework and the lake trail are the draw. Quiet in winter and cheap to stay in, which locals use.

name: Homesteads Tower Museum
unique: A stone water tower at the center of a 1930s federal resettlement community, with a museum in its base about the three hundred families who were given land and a house during the Depression.
buzz: The tower view over the homesteads is worth the climb and the museum is better than its size. One of the few places that explains a New Deal program by showing the actual houses around it.

name: Cumberland County Playhouse
unique: A professional theater on the banks of the Obey River that has been running musicals and plays since 1963, with a summer season that draws actors from New York and audiences from three states.
buzz: People are startled by the quality out here. The summer musicals sell out and the riverside setting makes an evening of it.

name: Ozone Falls
company: Tennessee Department of Environment and Conservation
unique: A state natural area where Fall Creek drops about a hundred feet over a sandstone lip into a plunge pool, a few hundred yards from Interstate 40.
buzz: The easiest big waterfall stop on the plateau. The trail down to the pool is steep and slick, and the top overlook is a two minute walk.

name: Crossville Historic Downtown
unique: A downtown of sandstone buildings on the plateau, built from local quarries, with antique shops, a bakery and a courthouse square that still holds the county's business.
buzz: The sandstone block and the antique stores are the draw. Crossville has become a retirement and second home town, and downtown has followed.

name: Sgt. Alvin C. York State Historic Park
unique: The farm, mill and grave of Alvin York, the Tennessee conscientious objector who captured 132 German soldiers in 1918 and came home to run a gristmill and a school in the same hollow.
buzz: The mill still runs and the rangers tell the story without hero worship. The drive down into Pall Mall is half the experience.

name: Big South Fork National River and Recreation Area
unique: A hundred and twenty five thousand acres of gorge country on the Cumberland River with natural arches, waterfalls, a preserved coal mining community and more than three hundred miles of horse trail.
buzz: The arches and the river gorge are the equal of any national park in the east with a fraction of the people. Riders and paddlers treat it as a yearly trip.

name: Allardt Great Pumpkin Festival
unique: A small town founded by German and Swiss immigrants that throws an October pumpkin festival with a giant pumpkin drop, crafts and food in a village of stone houses.
buzz: The pumpkin drop is the event and the crowd is bigger than the town. Get there early, the parking is in fields.

name: Jamestown Courthouse Square
unique: The seat of one of the poorest and most remote counties in Tennessee, a small square where the roads to the Big South Fork, Pall Mall and the Kentucky line all meet.
buzz: A supply stop rather than a destination, and that is useful when you are heading into the gorge country.

name: Pickett CCC Memorial State Park
unique: A Civilian Conservation Corps park of sandstone arches, caves and cliffs that was the first park in the southeast certified as a dark sky viewing location, so the Milky Way is visible from the ball field.
buzz: The arches and Hazard Cave are the hikes and the night sky is the reason astronomers drive out. The CCC cabins and stonework are intact.

name: Cordell Hull Birthplace State Park
unique: A log cabin reproduction and museum for Cordell Hull, the Tennessee congressman who wrote the legislation creating the United Nations and won the Nobel Peace Prize for it, on the farm where he was born.
buzz: A Nobel laureate from a hollow in Pickett County is a story most visitors have never heard. The short trail and picnic area make it an easy stop.

name: Standing Stone State Park
unique: A CCC era park from 1937 on the Highland Rim with a lake built for the mill and the town that were flooded to make it, stone cabins and a swimming beach in the woods.
buzz: Quiet, cheap cabins and a lake with no crowds. The story of the drowned town underneath is the local ghost story.

name: Overton County Courthouse Square
unique: A square with the courthouse, a monument and a row of shops in a county that sits on the edge of the plateau, halfway between Nashville and Knoxville on Highway 111.
buzz: A useful lunch stop and nothing more. The people are friendly and the square is intact.

name: Wilder Highway 111 Plateau Run
unique: The Highway 111 descent off the Cumberland Plateau between Livingston and Sparta, a long four lane grade with rock cuts, overlooks and a thousand feet of elevation change in a few miles.
buzz: Riders treat it as one of the best pieces of road in the state. The pull offs look over the valley toward the plateau wall.

name: Dale Hollow Lake
unique: A deep clear Corps lake on the Kentucky line with standing timber, smallmouth and walleye, and shoreline campgrounds that stay quiet even in July.
buzz: Anglers rate it for smallmouth and the water clarity is unusual for the region. Houseboat rentals fill in summer.
